assertions.statement: ChauffeurNet, an RNN model, uses mid-level input representations to output driving trajectories.
ChauffeurNet enables training on both real and simulated data.
ChauffeurNet facilitates closed-loop simulation testing prior to real vehicle deployment.
The CARLA simulator is an open-source platform designed for autonomous driving research.
CARLA supports development, training, and validation of urban driving systems.
CARLA supports flexible sensor suite and environmental condition specifications.
CARLA provides free urban environment content such as layouts, vehicles, buildings, and pedestrians.
CARLA offers measurements of agent state and traffic rule compliance.
End-to-end learning approaches include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that learn the entire processing pipeline to steer an automobile directly from single front-facing center camera images.
CNNs generate steering commands.
CARLA has been used to study end-to-end imitation learning alongside other autonomous driving approaches.
CARLA supports training and validation of perception and control models.
The CNN-based end-to-end method and the RNN-based mid-level representation method differ fundamentally in their input and output representations.
The CNN generates steering commands directly from raw images.
ChauffeurNet outputs driving trajectories based on mid-level inputs.
ChauffeurNet incorporates components such as FeatureNet and AgentRNN.
ChauffeurNet has recurrent feedback mechanisms to improve predictions.
Simulation platforms like CARLA align well with mid-level representation approaches by enabling controlled scenario evaluation.
Simulation platforms like CARLA enable closed-loop testing before real-world deployment.
There is a lack of direct empirical comparison between end-to-end CNN and mid-level RNN approaches under consistent conditions or datasets.
Pure imitation learning has been found insufficient even with large datasets and mid-level representations.
This insufficiency is due to error accumulation and distribution shift during closed-loop operation.
It remains unclear whether end-to-end approaches overcome the limitations of pure imitation learning.
There is a gap in understanding the comparative effectiveness of different imitation learning strategies.
